description: Unauthorized Data Access via S3 Buckets Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies, misconfigured bucket policies, or leaked credentials to access sensitive data stored in S3 buckets. Cross-account access and IAM role assumption could also be attack vectors. An attacker with compromised credentials or through a misconfigured IAM policy could list and download objects from the S3 buckets, accessing sensitive raw or processed data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement VPC endpoints for S3 access to ensure traffic doesn't traverse the public internet
recommendation: Implement strict bucket policies and enforce encryption
recommendation: Enable S3 access logging and implement automated monitoring

description: Insufficient Input Validation in Lambda Functions Lambda functions processing data without proper validation could be vulnerable to malformed input, leading to processing errors, resource exhaustion, or injection attacks in downstream systems. An attacker could submit maliciously crafted data through S3 or Kinesis that causes the Lambda functions to crash, consume excessive resources, or propagate malicious data to downstream systems.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Add rate limiting and throttling
recommendation: Implement circuit breakers and fallback mechanisms

description: Inadequate DDoS Protection Attackers could overwhelm the pipeline by sending large volumes of data through Kinesis or S3, triggering excessive Lambda executions and consuming available resources. An attacker could flood the Kinesis stream with data or rapidly upload many files to S3, causing increased costs and potential service disruption.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1498 - Network Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement AWS Shield and WAF
recommendation: Configure service quotas and limits
recommendation: Implement throttling and backoff mechanisms

description: Insecure Step Functions State Machine Configuration Misconfigured Step Functions could expose sensitive data in execution history, allow unauthorized execution starts, or enable manipulation of state transitions. An attacker with access to the Step Functions execution history could extract sensitive data passed between states or manipulate execution flow through unauthorized API calls.
references: recommendation: Secure sensitive data in transit

description: Unauthenticated Data Sources Without proper source authentication, attackers could inject unauthorized data into the pipeline through Kinesis streams or S3 uploads. An attacker could impersonate a legitimate data source and inject malicious or incorrect data into the processing pipeline.
